# zhbgvx

> Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex generalized Hermitian-definite banded eigenproblem A\*x = lambda\*B\*x.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhbgvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhbgvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhbgvx(
    order,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N, ka, kb,
    AB, LDAB,
    BB, LDBB,
    Q, LDQ,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    RWORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | `'all'`, `'value'`, or `'index'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `ka` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `ka ≥ 0` | number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of A |
| `kb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka` | number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of B |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `ka + 1 × N` |  | band matrix A in band storage (complex elements) |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAB ≥ ka + 1`; row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AB` |
| `BB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `kb + 1 × N` |  | band matrix B in band storage (complex elements) |
| ↳ `LDBB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDBB ≥ kb + 1`; row-major requires `LDBB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `BB` |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × N` |  | output transformation matrix (N-by-N) (complex elements) |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldq < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldq < N)` | leading dimension of `Q` |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ))` | index of smallest eigenvalue (1-based) |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue (1-based) |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute tolerance |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `w` |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvectors (complex elements) |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` | leading dimension of `Z` |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | complex workspace |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 7 * N` |  | real workspace |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output failure indices |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found;
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found;
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `ka`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KA} \ge 0$.
- `kb`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix B if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KB} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first ka+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(ka+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{ka}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{ka})$.

  On exit, the contents of `AB` are destroyed.
- `BB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix B, stored in the first kb+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of B is stored in the j-th column of the array `BB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BB(kb+1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kb}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BB(1+i-j,j) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kb})$.

  On exit, the factor S from the split Cholesky factorization $B = S^H \, S$, as returned by ZPBSTF.
- `Q`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, the n-by-n matrix used in the reduction of $A \, x = (\lambda ) \, B \, x$ to standard form, i.e. $C \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$, and consequently C to tridiagonal form. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, the array Q is not referenced.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing AP to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the matrix Z of eigenvectors, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. The eigenvectors are normalized so that $Z^H \, B \, Z = I$. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument is invalid (rejected when `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka`)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `ka + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `kb + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDQ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDQ < N )`)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-third argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-third argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhbgvx.ndarray(
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N, ka, kb,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    BB, strideBB1, strideBB2, offsetBB,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | `'all'`, `'value'`, or `'index'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `ka` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `ka ≥ 0` | number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of A |
| `kb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka` | number of super- (or sub-) diagonals of B |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `ka + 1 × N` |  | band matrix A in band storage (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `AB` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `AB` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AB` (complex elements) |
| `BB` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `kb + 1 × N` |  | band matrix B in band storage (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideBB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `BB` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideBB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `BB` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetBB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `BB` (complex elements) |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × N` |  | output transformation matrix (N-by-N) (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `Q` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `Q` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Q` (complex elements) |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ))` | index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for w |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvector matrix (N-by-M) (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of first dimension of Z (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of second dimension of Z (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for Z (complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | complex workspace (length >= N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ 7 * N` |  | real workspace (length >= 7*N) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for RWORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace (length >= 5*N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IWORK |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IFAIL |
| ↳ `offsetIFAIL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IFAIL |

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `kb < 0 \|\| kb > ka`)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-first argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-second argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `7 * N` elements from `offsetRWork`
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `5 * N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is: \<= N:  then i eigenvectors failed to converge.  Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.
-   `> N`: if $\mathrm{INFO} = N + i$, for $1 \le i \le N$, then ZPBSTF returned `INFO = i`: B is not positive definite. The factorization of B could not be completed and no eigenvalues or eigenvectors were computed.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zhbgvx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHBGVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zhbgvx.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable no-restricted-syntax, stdlib/first-unit-test */

import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zhbgvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhbgvx';

// 5x5 Hermitian band matrix A (KA=2), upper band storage (interleaved re/im):
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const AB = new Complex128Array([
	0,
	0,
	0,
	0,
	10,
	0,
	0,
	0,
	1,
	0.5,
	8,
	0,
	0.5,
	0.1,
	2,
	-0.3,
	6,
	0,
	0.3,
	-0.2,
	1.5,
	0.2,
	9,
	0,
	0.4,
	0.15,
	1,
	-0.4,
	7,
	0
]);

// 5x5 Hermitian positive definite band matrix B (KB=1), upper storage:
const BB = new Complex128Array([
	0,
	0,
	4,
	0,
	0.2,
	0.1,
	5,
	0,
	0.3,
	-0.1,
	3,
	0,
	0.1,
	0.05,
	6,
	0,
	0.2,
	-0.1,
	4,
	0
]);

const Q = new Complex128Array( 25 );
const W = new Float64Array( 5 );
const Z = new Complex128Array( 25 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 10 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 50 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 30 );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( 5 );

// Compute all eigenvalues and eigenvectors:
const info = zhbgvx.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', 5, 2, 1, AB, 1, 3, 0, BB, 1, 2, 0, Q, 1, 5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, m, W, 1, 0, Z, 1, 5, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, IFAIL, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );       // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'M:', m[ 0 ] );         // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Eigenvalues:', W );   // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHBGVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHBGVX computes all the eigenvalues, and optionally, the eigenvectors of a complex generalized Hermitian-definite banded eigenproblem, of the form $A \, x=(\lambda ) \, B \, x$. Here A and B are assumed to be Hermitian and banded, and B is also positive definite. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either all eigenvalues, a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>
